# Worker Agents Skills

This repository bundles the baseline skills installed by [Worker
Agents](https://github.com/agents-dev/workerAgents).

The bundled skills are available under [`skills/`](skills/):

- `mcp-duckgo` — imported from `aahl/skills@mcp-duckgo`.
- `image-search` — imported from `z0gsh1u/oh-my-writing-skill@image-search`.
- `gauntlet-loop` — imported from `robonuggets/gauntlet-loop@gauntlet-loop`.
- `load-sketchfab-threejs` — local asset inspection, normalization, and Three.js/PlayCanvas A/B viewer skill.
- `opencode-zen-completions` — use the OpenCode Zen chat completions API for implementation work.

The original upstream licenses are preserved in
[`third-party-licenses/`](third-party-licenses/).
name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment.

name: three-game-discovery
description: Find newly created browser games, especially Three.js and GPT-6 Astra projects, and verify that repositories are non-empty, playable-looking, and actually use Three.js.
---

# Three.js game discovery

Use this skill when the user asks to find new browser games, Three.js games, or games made with GPT-6 Astra.

The skill registry is [games.json](games.json). Treat it as a durable append-only discovery list. Do not add a repository until verification accepts it.

## Define the date

Use UTC for repository timestamps. Treat “today” as the current UTC date unless the user gives another date. Separate these meanings:

- `created:` means the GitHub repository was created on that date.
- `pushed:` means an older repository changed on that date.
- Google `after:` and `before:` describe search-index timing, not repository creation.

## Use the high-yield search order

1. Run `scripts/search_github_games.py` with the target date. It combines the focused queries that produced the best results:
   - `three.js game in:description`
   - `threejs game in:description`
   - `"React Three Fiber" game in:description`
   - `webgpu game in:description`
   - `"GPT-6 Astra" in:description`
   - `"GPT-Astra" in:description`
2. Run `scripts/verify_github_games.py` on the result file. Keep only repositories with a non-empty tree and source evidence for Three.js. The verifier automatically upserts accepted records into `games.json`.
3. Inspect the README, package manifest, and a small set of source files. Require one of these markers: `THREE.`, `THREE.WebGLRenderer`, `from 'three'`, `three.module.js`, or `@react-three/`.
4. Classify a project as a game only when its description, README, or source has game evidence such as a player, level, enemy, racer, shooter, physics game, or playable controls. Do not count museums, dashboards, prompt packs, catalogs, or generic Three.js demos as games.
5. For ASTRA, Opus, and Fable attribution, record the name only when the repository description or README mentions it. Do not infer model attribution from a repository name alone. Mark catalog-only attribution as lower confidence.

## Use these secondary searches

Use Google only for discovery and use GitHub metadata for date verification:

```text
site:github.com/ ("Three.js" OR "three.module.js" OR "@react-three/fiber") (game OR playable OR racer OR shooter) after:YYYY-MM-DD before:YYYY-MM-DD
site:github.io/ ("Three.js" OR "React Three Fiber") (game OR play OR playable) after:YYYY-MM-DD before:YYYY-MM-DD
site:github.com/ ("GPT-6 Astra" OR "GPT-Astra") ("Three.js" OR "React Three Fiber") (game OR racer OR shooter)
```

Use GH Archive when GitHub search has not indexed a new repository. The archive finds public `CreateEvent` repository events, but it does not prove that the repository is a game. Hydrate each candidate with the GitHub API and then run the verifier. The helper `scripts/gh_archive_candidates.py` reads one hourly archive file at a time.

## Handle limits correctly

Do not rotate accounts to evade GitHub rate limits. Check the limit, stop or wait when necessary, and continue with Google, GH Archive, public repository pages, or previously collected candidates. Never print tokens or credentials.

## Report results

For each accepted result, report the repository link, UTC creation time, game type, star count, content language, programming language, engine, model attribution, Three.js evidence, and confidence. Report exclusions briefly when they explain a false positive, such as empty, Canvas 2D, Godot, catalog-only, or non-game.

## Registry fields

Write one object per accepted repository. Use these fields:

- `date`: UTC repository creation date.
- `repo`: `OWNER/REPO`.
- `star_count`: GitHub star count at discovery time.
- `language`: `Chinese`, `English`, `Other`, or `Unknown` for repository text.
- `programming_language`: GitHub's primary language.
- `engine`: canonical engine such as `Three.js`, `PlayCanvas`, `Godot`, `Unity`, `Unreal Engine`, `Babylon.js`, `Phaser`, or `Unknown`.
- `created_with`: optional list containing only `Astra`, `Opus`, or `Fable` when evidence exists.
- `evidence`: sampled paths and matching markers.

Use `--no-save` only for a dry run. Normal verification must update the registry automatically.

## Helper scripts

```text
python3 scripts/discover_games.py --date 2026-09-08 --output verified.json
python3 scripts/search_github_games.py --date 2026-09-08 --output candidates.json
python3 scripts/verify_github_games.py --input candidates.json --output verified.json
python3 scripts/verify_github_games.py --repo OWNER/REPO --registry games.json
python3 scripts/gh_archive_candidates.py --date 2026-09-08 --hour 3
```

The scripts require the `gh` CLI for GitHub API calls. They use one authenticated account at a time and do not implement account rotation.

# Issue E2E kickoff

Use only for an explicitly requested issue-triggered E2E run. Always create a
new issue and Action for each invocation. Never reuse, continue, edit, or
inspect an existing matching issue or run as a substitute. Then stop at the
initial Web UI link. Do not claim implementation completion.

## Write the issue prompt

Locate the skill invocation in the user's message. Remove only the invocation
syntax and routing metadata such as `#main` and mode labels. Keep the surrounding
request text in its original order.

If `#c` is present, drop `#c` and all routing metadata, then copy the remaining
request text exactly as the issue body. Set the issue title to the remaining text. Attach `OpenCode`. Do not read the rubric, rewrite the
text, add a heading, or add a skills sentence.

Read `references/gauntlet-prompt-rubric.md` whenever the remaining request is
sparse, names only a product or concept, lacks a concrete quality bar, or does
not state the required output surface and dimensionality. Rewrite that request
as a concise Gauntlet Loop prompt. Never let invocation placement bypass the
rubric.

If the invocation has no request text, invent a fresh random small playable
browser-game brief. Do not substitute a generic workflow-validation task or
ask the user for a game concept.

Keep the title and visible body limited to the user request. Attach `OpenCode`.
Store branch routing in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment.

Write the issue body to a temporary Markdown file and pass it with
`gh issue create --body-file <path>` or `gh issue edit --body-file <path>`.
Do not interpolate Markdown containing backticks, `$`, `$(...)`, or backslashes
inside a shell double-quoted argument. Verify the saved body with
`gh issue view <number> --json title,body,labels` before checking the run.

Do not execute the full Gauntlet Loop during issue-e2e kickoff. The prompt
should instruct the worker to perform the sustained project work after the
issue starts.

Before writing the issue, list the target repository's `skill/*` labels and
select only the skills that directly support the request. Add one short
imperative sentence to the issue prompt that names the selected skills and
requires the worker to load and use them where relevant. Attach every selected
`skill/*` label when creating the issue so the workflow passes the same skill
names to OpenCode. For visual recreation work, prefer an available image-search
skill over generic web search. For 3D game work, select available 3D asset or
runtime skills only when they match the requested implementation.

With `#c`, still attach selected `skill/*` labels but do not alter the copied
title or body to name them.


Check `git branch --show-current`. If non-empty and not `main`, verify it and
set `branch` in the hidden request metadata. The reusable workflow checks
out the validated `target_sha` and uses `target_ref` as its result base, preserving the
debugging worktree. Default-branch preparation dispatches the listener at this
branch. Treat the selected-branch run as the execution run. This suffix is
routing metadata, not prompt text. On `main`, omit it.

Resolve the target repository before creating the issue. With `#main`, use the
current checkout repository on `main`.
Resolve that repository before listing labels or creating the issue. Do not use
the `AgentsLoop/PlayGround` fallback when `#main` is present. Otherwise, on
`main` without a supplied repository, use
`AgentsLoop/PlayGround` explicitly. On another branch, use the current
repository. Never infer the default `main` repository from `git remote`.

If the user mentions another local skill, verify it exists in
`https://github.com/denaidark/skills/` before selecting it. If it is absent,
push it first.

## Procedure

1. Check `git status --short` and the current branch; preserve unrelated work.

We'll build a game. Need to decide engine: plain HTML/JS + Three.js? The environment supports static HTML or Vite. It's a browser game. - Battle system with auto-resolve and animated combat maybe
- Commander/hero system
- Research/tech tree
- Quests/rewards

- Save/load localStorage
- Responsive

Given user asks in Portuguese, UI in Portuguese. Answer in Portuguese.

Could implement with Three.js for base rendering? The environment skill mentions Three.js. But complexity/time. A beautiful 2.5D canvas/CSS base might be more reliable and visually striking. Or Three.js low-poly base view with buildings rendered as meshes. Three.js via CDN or npm? Better install three and use Vite, since default-start supports Vite automatically. But screenshots capture static server. Vite builds. Install dependencies probably allowed (npm). Let's check network. We can use npm install three. That risks build time but fine.

Which approach gives best visual quality with manageable code? A hybrid: DOM/CSS UI + canvas/isometric base rendered in 2D with beautiful procedural art. Canvas 2D can look great with gradients, shadows, glows. No external assets needed. World map also canvas. Battle screen with animated units (canvas). This gives full control, performant, no dependency issues. Could still use Three.js for the base 3D, but need models. Procedural low-poly buildings in Three.js could look good but might look simplistic. A hand-crafted isometric canvas city can look like a polished strategy game.

I'll build vanilla JS ES modules + Vite (or pure static). Pure static with index.html + js modules served by the runtime works, and no build step. But capture uses start.sh default server which handles static. Pure static is simplest and reliable. However, if index.html exists at root, projectType returns 'html' and server serves it. Fine. Modules work over HTTP.

But maybe tests expected? There's no test harness. Need to run server and screenshots to verify. Capture script takes desktop/mobile screenshots after clicking start selector.

Core loop:
1. Base: buildings (Quartel General, Quartel, Fábrica de Petróleo, Siderúrgica, Fazenda, Depósito, Academia Militar, Hospital, Muralha, Radar). Each has level, upgrade costs/time, production.

Need progression to feel real, not static. Initial resources enough to do things, timers short (10-60s) so demo showcases loop.

Visual style: dark military, gold/amber accents, glass panels, top HUD with resources, left nav, isometric base in center. Use fonts from Google? ## Objective
- Build a browser strategy war game inspired by Gameloft's "War Planet Online": isometric base building, world map conquest, troops, research, heroes, campaign and animated battles, in Portuguese.
- User's exact request: "Crie um jogo igual war planeta online de guerra igual o da gameloft"

## Requirements
- Playable in-browser strategy war game with Portuguese (pt-BR) UI.
- Quality bar: polished, visually rich, AAA-feeling presentation.
- Scope: base construction/upgrades, world map with sectors, army training, research, heroes, missions, battles, save/load.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS ES modules + HTML/CSS, no build step (runtime serves static `index.html` directly).
- Procedural canvas art (no external game assets) for isometric base, world map, battle scene, title background.
- Local fonts downloaded to `assets/fonts/` (Barlow Condensed 600/700/800, Rajdhani 500/600/700) for offline fidelity.
- localStorage save with versioned schema (`comando-global-save-v3`), offline production, timers.
- Game title: "COMANDO GLOBAL — Guerra pelo Planeta".

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html` created: title screen, SVG icon sprite, HUD, nav rail, base/world/panel views, context panel, dock, modals/toasts/battle roots.
- `css/style.css` created: full design system, title screen, HUD, rail, stage, context, dock, world markers, army/research/campaign/hero/alliance views, modals, battle overlay, responsive mobile styles.
- `js/data.js` created: resource/building/unit/tech/hero/target/mission/ranking/chat data, cost/time formulas, formatting helpers, hero portrait SVG generator.
- `js/state.js` created: initial state, save/load/reset, event bus, economy/production/capacity/energy/power formulas, upgrade/build/train/research/hero actions, march/battle outcome computation, mission progress/claim, ticker, offline production.
- `js/audio.js` created: procedural WebAudio SFX, ambient drone, battle ambience, victory/defeat/explosion/gunfire sounds.
- Fixed duplicate player XP award in `resolveArrival`.

### Active
- `js/iso.js` (isometric base renderer) was being written; the write call failed because the payload exceeded the output token limit. No content was saved for this file.
- Still needed: `js/world.js` (world map renderer), `js/battle.js` (battle scene), `js/ui.js` (views/rendering/actions), `js/main.js` (boot/title/ticker wiring).

### Blocked
- `js/iso.js` must be written in smaller chunks (e.g., helpers + class skeleton first, then building draw methods) to avoid tool output limits.

## Next Move
1. Recreate `js/iso.js` incrementally with the isometric renderer: 11×11 plateau, roads, terrain, buildings (`hq`, `oil`, `steel`, `farm`, `power`, `barracks`, `factory`, `warehouse`, `lab`, `market`, `radar`, `airbase`, `hospital`, `wall`), empty plots, smoke/particles, flags, selection/hover hit-testing, screen-space level badges/progress.
2. Create `js/world.js`: canvas strategic map terrain, 18 markers (17 enemies + player base at 53,48), region styling, march lines/countdowns, conquest coloring, domination.
3. Create `js/battle.js`: animated battlefield canvas (soldiers/tanks/helicopters, tracers, explosions, screen shake), HUD bars/phase timer, skip, victory/defeat result overlay, calls `resolveArrival`.
4. Create `js/ui.js`: HUD/dock/context rendering, view routers for army/research/campaign/hero/alliance, modals (train/attack/reports/settings/more), event delegation, mobile context sheet, chat feed, toasts.
5. Create `js/main.js`: title background canvas, start/continue flow, audio init, renderer boot, ticker, `subscribe` wiring, battle auto-open on arrival, save restore.
6. Run `PORT=3002 ./start.sh` via tmux, then `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots CAPTURE_STRICT=1 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs"`; inspect desktop/mobile screenshots and iterate on visuals/bugs.
7. Update `README.md` with game description and controls; verify no console errors and responsive layout.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/index.html`: complete game shell, title screen, icon sprite, all view containers.
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/css/style.css`: all layout/visual styling; must match classes used by JS.
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/js/data.js`: canonical data and helpers used everywhere.

## Objective
- Build a browser strategy war game inspired by Gameloft's "War Planet Online": isometric base building, world map conquest, troops, research, heroes, campaign and animated battles, in Portuguese.
- User's exact request: "Crie um jogo igual war planeta online de guerra igual o da gameloft"

## Requirements
- Playable in-browser strategy war game with Portuguese (pt-BR) UI.
- Quality bar: polished, visually rich, AAA-feeling presentation.
- Scope: base construction/upgrades, world map with sectors, army training, research, heroes, missions, battles, save/load.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS ES modules + HTML/CSS, no build step (runtime serves static `index.html` directly).
- Procedural canvas art (no external game assets) for isometric base, world map, battle scene, title background.
- Local fonts downloaded to `assets/fonts/` (Barlow Condensed 600/700/800, Rajdhani 500/600/700) for offline fidelity.
- localStorage save with versioned schema (`comando-global-save-v3`), offline production, timers.
- Game title: "COMANDO GLOBAL — Guerra pelo Planeta".
- Canvas renderers read game state live rather than receiving snapshots; UI only needs to call `layout()`/`refresh()` after changes.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`: title screen, SVG icon sprite, HUD, nav rail, base/world/panel views, context panel, dock, modals/toasts/battle roots.
- `css/style.css`: full design system, title screen, HUD, rail, stage, context, dock, world markers, army/research/campaign/hero/alliance views, modals, battle overlay, responsive mobile styles.
- `js/data.js`: resources/building/unit/tech/hero/target/mission/ranking/chat data, cost/time formulas, formatting helpers, `heroPortrait` SVG generator.
- `js/state.js`: initial state, save/load/reset, event bus (`subscribe`/`emit`), economy/production/capacity/energy/power formulas, upgrade/build/train/research/hero actions, march/battle outcome computation, mission progress/claim, ticker, offline production.
- `js/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio SFX, ambient drone, battle ambience, victory/defeat/explosion/gunfire sounds.
- `js/iso.js`: complete `IsoRenderer` class — high-DPI resize, isometric projection and hit-testing, plateau/terrain/roads/plaza/fence/props, custom art for all 14 buildings plus unbuilt plots, smoke/flags/vehicles, selection/hover outlines, screen-space level/construction/production badges.
- `js/world.js`: complete `WorldRenderer` — static map offscreen render (ocean, continent, islands, faction glows, mountains, forests, rivers, roads, labels, grid), HTML markers for all 18 targets, radar sweep, selection routes, animated march convoys/countdowns, conquest marker refresh.
- `js/battle.js`: complete `BattleScene` — animated sky/ground, ruins, searchlights, friendly/enemy infantry/tanks/helicopters, tracers, explosions, sparks, screen shake, phase/timer HUD, health bars, skip, result overlay, battle audio, calls `onFinish` after result.
- `js/ui.js`: complete `UI` class — HUD resources/energy/power/badge, dock build/train/research/march slots with progress, context panels for base buildings and world targets, army/research/campaign/hero/alliance views, train/attack/reports/settings/more/reset modals, toasts, chat feed, mobile context sheet, state subscriptions, battle queue, timer updates.

### Active
- `js/main.js` has not been created yet; `index.html` imports `js/main.js`, so the game currently fails to boot.
- Need to wire renderers + UI, title screen canvas/start flow, ticker, battle finish callback, chat/form listeners, save/arrival restore.

### Blocked
- None technical; `js/main.js` is the only missing module.

## Next Move
1. Create `js/main.js`: import state/audio/renderers/UI; `loadState()`; instantiate `BattleScene` with callback calling `ui.battleFinished(outcome)`; instantiate `IsoRenderer`, `WorldRenderer`, `UI`; wire title canvas animation and `#btn-start` flow (`title-screen.leaving`, `#game.ready`, `initAudio`, `startTicker`); apply saved view; open pending battle from `activeBattle()`; save on `beforeunload`.
2. Add missing UI wiring in `js/main.js`/`js/ui.js`: chat form submit handler (`#chat-form`, `#chat-input`), Escape/backdrop works, title continue label when save exists, sound/music initial application.
3. Fix any obvious issues found by static review: unused imports in `world.js` (`targetState`) and `battle.js` (`UNIT_BY_KEY`, `march` unused), `ui.js` progress bar in `worldContext` uses `progressBar(0,1)` (renders 100% incorrectly), `click`/`close` imports.
4. Start server with `PORT=3002 ./start.sh` in background/tmux; run `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3002 CAPTURE_DIR=screenshots CAPTURE_STRICT=1 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-capture.mjs"`.
5. Inspect desktop/mobile screenshots; iterate on visual fidelity/layout bugs and responsive behavior.
6. Update `README.md` with game description and controls; verify no console errors, title→game transition, building selection, train/research/attack flows, battle overlay, save/load.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/index.html`: complete game shell; imports `js/main.js`; title screen, sprite IDs, view containers.
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/css/style.css`: all styling/classes used by JS; add `.ctx-mobile-close` base style if needed (currently only mobile rule).
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/js/state.js`: canonical rules/state; exports actions used by UI; `SAVE_KEY='comando-global-save-v3'`; `resolveArrival(id)`, `activeBattle()`, ticker.
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/js/data.js`: canonical data/formulas/format helpers; `TARGETS`, `MISSIONS`, `HERO_DEFS`, `heroPortrait`.
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/js/ui.js`: UI class; main integration surface (`battleFinished`, `renderAll`, `applyView`).
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/js/iso.js`: `IsoRenderer` (`start`, `stop`, `resize`, `layout`, `select`).
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/js/world.js`: `WorldRenderer` (`start`, `stop`, `resize`, `refresh`, `setSelected`).
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/js/battle.js`: `BattleScene` (`play(outcome)`, `active`, callback `onFinish`).
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/js/audio.js`: `initAudio`, sound/music toggles, battle SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/assets/fonts/`: local WOFF2 fonts referenced by CSS.
- `/home/runner/work/Batalha/Batalha/start.sh`: starts static runtime server (`PORT` env respected).

## Important Context
- `state.js` exports live binding `state`; renderers import it directly, so level/ownership changes require only `iso.layout()` / `world.refresh()`.
- Base layout (2×2 footprints on 11×11 grid): hq `4,4`; oil `1,1`; farm `1,8`; steel `4,8`; power `7,1`; barracks `4,1`; factory `8,4`; warehouse `6,8`; lab `2,3`; market `8,8`; radar `0,6`; airbase `9,1`; hospital `4,6`; wall `0,4`.
- Starting levels: hq 3, oil/steel/farm/power/barracks 2, factory/warehouse/lab 1; market/airbase/radar/hospital/wall level 0.
- Isometric projection: `sx=(x-y)*32`, `sy=(x+y)*16`; plateau 0..11, earth depth ~46 px.
- Enemy targets use percentage positions; player base at `(53,48)`; `targetTravel` ≈ 6–16s. Target defense 900–32,000; initial army power ≈4,000–5,500 so early sectors are beatable.
- March slots = 2, builder slots = 2, training queue max 3, research queue max 1.
- `state.arrivals` holds pending outcomes; `emit('arrival', outcome)` fires; UI queues battle and calls `resolveArrival` in `battleFinished`.
- `resolveArrival` returns `{report,outcome}` and applies survivors/loot/XP; result overlay shows outcome before it is applied.
- Panel views use `#game.wide` (hides context); mobile ≤900px uses bottom rail, fixed context sheet `.open`, dock hidden.
- `#game.ready` must be added after start; title button `aria-label="Play"` with visible text "ENTRAR NA GUERRA".
- Runtime capture uses `CAPTURE_URL`, `CAPTURE_DIR`, `CAPTURE_STRICT` with `scripts/default-capture.mjs`; screenshots directory should be created/inspected.

## Objective
- Build a browser strategy war game inspired by Gameloft's "War Planet Online": isometric base building, world map conquest, troops, research, heroes, campaign and animated battles, in Portuguese.
- User's exact request: "Crie um jogo igual war planeta online de guerra igual o da gameloft"

## Requirements
- Playable in-browser strategy war game with Portuguese (pt-BR) UI.
- Quality bar: polished, visually rich, AAA-feeling presentation.
- Scope: base construction/upgrades, world map with sectors, army training, research, heroes, missions, battles, save/load.

## Decisions
- Vanilla JS ES modules + HTML/CSS, no build step; runtime serves static `index.html`.
- Procedural canvas art (no external game assets) for isometric base, world map, battle scene, title background.
- Local fonts in `assets/fonts/` for offline fidelity.
- localStorage save with versioned schema (`comando-global-save-v3`), offline production, timers.
- Game title: "COMANDO GLOBAL — Guerra pelo Planeta".
- Mobile layout uses bottom rail, hidden dock, fixed bottom-sheet context panel; title start allowed to auto-click for capture.

## Work State
### Completed
- `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/data.js`, `js/state.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/iso.js`, `js/world.js`, `js/battle.js`, `js/ui.js` implemented.

# COMANDO GLOBAL — Guerra pelo Planeta

Jogo de estratégia de guerra em tempo real para navegador, em português. Construa uma base militar isométrica, evolua edifícios, treine exércitos, pesquise tecnologias, recrute comandantes e conquiste setores no mapa do planeta.

Inspirado nos clássicos jogos de construção de base e conquista territorial para dispositivos móveis, mas feito para rodar direto no navegador — sem instalação, sem build e sem assets externos de jogo.

![Base isométrica](screenshots/final-desktop.png)

## Recursos

- **Base isométrica procedural** com 14 construções: quartel-general, petróleo, fazenda, aço, energia, quartel, fábrica, armazém, laboratório, mercado, radar, base aérea, hospital e muralha.
- **Economia em tempo real** com produção por hora, capacidade de armazenamento, coleta manual, custos e fila de obras.
- **Exército com 5 classes** — infantaria, tanques, artilharia, helicópteros e unidades de elite — com treino em fila e capacidade de tropas.
- **Pesquisa bélica** com 8 tecnologias em ramos econômico e militar.
- **3 comandantes (heróis)** com habilidades, níveis, pontos e bônus de combate.
- **Campanha com 8 missões**, recompensas e objetivos progressivos.
- **Mapa-múndi com 18 setores**, facções, níveis de ameaça, probabilidade de vitória, marchas e conquista permanente.
- **Batalhas animadas** em canvas, com unidades, disparos, explosões, resultado, perdas, saque e relatórios.
- **Aliança** com membros, ranking e chat funcional.
- **Salvamento local** automático, produção offline (até 6 horas), filas persistentes e retomada de batalhas pendentes.
- **Interface responsiva** para desktop, tablet e celular, com painel contextual em bottom sheet no mobile.
- **Áudio procedural** via Web Audio API (efeitos e ambiente), sem arquivos de áudio.
- **Arte 100% procedural** em canvas, com fontes locais para funcionar offline.

## Como jogar

1. **Base** — clique/tap em um edifício para abrir o painel de comando. Evolua o quartel-general para liberar níveis maiores; construa e evolua os demais edifícios para aumentar produção, capacidade e poder.
2. **Exército** — treine unidades no painel do exército. Cada classe tem custo, tempo e poder diferentes. Use **MAX** para preencher a capacidade disponível.
3. **Pesquisa** — invista recursos no laboratório para obter bônus permanentes de economia e combate.
4. **Mundo** — escolha um setor inimigo, confira a defesa e a probabilidade de vitória, monte a força de ataque e envie a marcha. Ao chegar, a batalha começa automaticamente.
5. **Heróis** — selecione o comandante ativo e distribua pontos de habilidade ganhos em batalhas.
6. **Campanha e aliança** — no desktop, use os botões da barra lateral. No celular, toque em **MAIS** para acessar campanha, aliança, relatórios e configurações.
7. **Relatórios** — o ícone de correio no topo mostra batalhas, perdas, saques e recompensas.

### Controles

- **Mouse / toque:** selecionar edifícios, setores, unidades e ações.
- **Teclas 1–7:** alternar entre Base, Mundo, Exército, Pesquisa, Herói, Campanha e Aliança.
- **Esc:** fechar modal/painel ou voltar ao mapa da base.
- **Botões + / − / centralizar:** controlar o zoom e a posição do mapa-múndi.

## Executar localmente

O projeto é estático e usa ES Modules. Não há etapa de build.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Abra `http://localhost:8000`.

Também é possível usar o script de inicialização do ambiente:

```bash
./start.sh
```

Para entrar direto no jogo (útil para demonstrações e capturas automatizadas), acrescente `?autostart=1` à URL.

## Estrutura

```text
index.html          # shell da interface e sprite SVG de ícones
css/style.css       # layout desktop/mobile, tema e animações
js/data.js          # definições de edifícios, unidades, tecnologias, heróis e setores
js/state.js         # estado do jogo, regras, economia, filas, marchas, salvamento
js/iso.js           # renderização isométrica da base
js/world.js         # mapa-múndi e marcadores de setores
js/battle.js        # cena de batalha animada em canvas
js/ui.js            # HUD, painéis, modais, contexto móvel, chat e relatórios
js/audio.js         # efeitos e ambiente procedural via Web Audio
js/main.js          # tela-título, inicialização, ticker e atalhos
assets/fonts/       # Barlow Condensed e Rajdhani (offline)
```

## Persistência

O progresso é salvo no `localStorage` sob a chave `comando-global-save-v3`. O jogo aplica produção offline ao reabrir e retoma batalhas que chegaram enquanto a aba estava fechada. Para apagar o progresso, use **Configurações → Reiniciar operação**.

## Créditos

- Código, arte procedural e áudio: projeto original.
- Fontes: Barlow Condensed e Rajdhani (SIL Open Font License).
- Inspiração de gênero: jogos de estratégia de base e conquista global. Este é um projeto independente, sem afiliação com marcas ou estúdios citados.

## O que foi construído

- **Base isométrica** com 14 edifícios, evolução, energia, coleta e fila de obras.
- **Economia em tempo real** com produção por hora, capacidade e salvamento offline.
- **Exército** com 5 classes de unidades, treino em fila e limite de tropas.
- **Pesquisa bélica** com 8 tecnologias.
- **3 comandantes** com habilidades e evolução.
- **Campanha** com 8 missões e recompensas.
- **Mapa-múndi** com 18 setores, facções, marchas e conquista permanente.
- **Batalhas animadas** em canvas, com resultado, perdas, saque e relatórios.
- **Aliança**, chat, ranking, relatórios e configurações.
- **Interface responsiva** para desktop, tablet e celular.
- **Arte e áudio 100% procedurais**, fontes locais e nenhuma dependência externa.

## Controles

- **Mouse/toque:** selecionar edifícios, setores e ações.
- **Teclas 1–7:** Base, Mundo, Exército, Pesquisa, Herói, Campanha e Aliança.
- **Esc:** fecha painéis/modais ou volta para a base.
- **Celular:** a barra inferior mostra **MAIS**, com acesso a campanha, aliança, relatórios e configurações.

## Como executar

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Depois abra `http://localhost:8000`. Também é possível usar `./start.sh`. Para entrar direto no jogo em demonstrações, use `?autostart=1`.

## Verificação realizada

- Sintaxe de todos os módulos JS validada.
- Captura automatizada desktop/mobile concluída sem erros de console.
- Fluxos testados: início, evolução de QG, treino, pesquisa, ataque pelo mapa, batalha, vitória, conquista do setor, chat, recarregamento e persistência do save.
- Layout mobile/tablet validado sem overflow horizontal, com painel contextual, modais e batalha ajustados à tela.
